feed.title: Pronounce — recent dictionary additions
feed.subtitle: How engineers actually pronounce project / product / jargon names. Community-maintained.

entry.title: interoception — in ter oh SEP shun
entry.summary: interoception is pronounced "in ter oh SEP shun" (/ˌɪntəroʊˈsɛpʃən/). The sensing of internal bodily signals such as heartbeat, breathing, and hunger; increasingly used in embodied-agent and computational-emotion models. Say in-ter-oh-SEP-shun.

entry.title: alexithymia — uh lek sih THIGH mee uh
entry.summary: alexithymia is pronounced "uh lek sih THIGH mee uh" (/əˌlɛksɪˈθaɪmiə/). Difficulty identifying or describing emotions, used in affect-recognition research and human-AI evaluation. Primary stress lands on THIGH: uh-lek-sih-THIGH-mee-uh.

entry.title: affordance — uh FOR dunce
entry.summary: affordance is pronounced "uh FOR dunce" (/əˈfɔːrdəns/). An action possibility offered by an environment to an agent; central to robotics, embodied AI, and action-aware world models. Stress FOR: uh-FOR-duhns.

entry.title: homeostasis — hoh mee oh STAY sis
entry.summary: homeostasis is pronounced "hoh mee oh STAY sis" (/ˌhoʊmioʊˈsteɪsɪs/). The regulation of internal stability; a useful framing for agents that model needs, drives, affect, and bodily state. Five syllables, with primary stress on STAY: hoh-mee-oh-STAY-sis.

entry.title: enactivism — ih NAK tih viz um
entry.summary: enactivism is pronounced "ih NAK tih viz um" (/ɪˈnæktɪvɪzəm/). A cognitive-science view in which cognition emerges through an agent's embodied interaction with its environment rather than passive representation alone. Say ih-NAK-tiv-iz-um.

entry.title: autopoiesis — aw toh poy EE sis
entry.summary: autopoiesis is pronounced "aw toh poy EE sis" (/ˌɔːtoʊpɔɪˈiːsɪs/). Self-production or self-maintenance in living systems, closely tied to enactive cognition and autonomous-agent theory. The final three syllables are poy-EE-sis, with primary stress on EE.

entry.title: Genie 3 — jee nee three
entry.summary: Genie 3 is pronounced "jee nee three" (/ˈdʒiːni ˈθriː/). Google DeepMind's real-time interactive world model, announced in 2025 and opened through Project Genie in 2026. The name is the ordinary word "genie" followed by the numeral: JEE-nee three.

entry.title: Marble — mar bul
entry.summary: Marble is pronounced "mar bul" (/ˈmɑːrbəl/). World Labs' multimodal model for creating editable, explorable 3D worlds from text, images, video, or layouts. Say MAR-buhl, like the ordinary English word.

entry.title: humans& — humans and
entry.summary: humans& is pronounced "humans and" (/ˈhjuːmənz ænd/). Human-centric AI lab; the ampersand is read as the word "and" per its own domain humansand.ai and @humansand handle.

entry.title: Boba — boh buh
entry.summary: Boba is pronounced "boh buh" (/ˈboʊbə/). humans& social AI agent companion (launched Oct 2026); named after the drink, read like it: BOH-buh.

entry.title: &Tutor — ampersand tutor
entry.summary: &Tutor is pronounced "ampersand tutor" (/ˈæmpərˌsænd ˈtuːtər/). humans& tutor model; its own announcement expands "&Tutor" to "Ampersand Tutor", so & reads ampersand here, not "and".

entry.title: Persimmon — per sim uhn
entry.summary: Persimmon is pronounced "per sim uhn" (/pərˈsɪmən/). humans&'s large-scale user model simulating human chat behavior; a deliberate fruit name read as ordinary English.

entry.title: Ampersand — am per sand
entry.summary: Ampersand is pronounced "am per sand" (/ˈæmpərˌsænd/). humans&'s first collaborator model (Oct 2026, Agents API); named after the & character, ordinary English reading.

entry.title: TutorMoments — tutor moments
entry.summary: TutorMoments is pronounced "tutor moments" (/ˈtuːtər ˌmoʊmənts/). Ai2 benchmark scoring AI tutors on real tutoring decision moments; plain English compound tutor + moments.

entry.title: MegaMoE — MEG uh em oh EE
entry.summary: MegaMoE is pronounced "MEG uh em oh EE" (/ˈmɛɡə ˌɛm oʊ ˈiː/). Distributed MoE decode kernel from humans& (in FlashInfer and SGLang); mega + MoE, inheriting MoE's spelled-out vs "moh" split.

entry.title: 4-bitter Lesson — four bitter lesson
entry.summary: 4-bitter Lesson is pronounced "four bitter lesson" (/ˌfɔːrˈbɪtər ˈlɛsən/). humans& pun on Sutton's Bitter Lesson for its 4-bit RL recipe; reads four-BIT-ter LESS-un.

entry.title: Multi-User Turing Test — mul tee yoo zer touring test
entry.summary: Multi-User Turing Test is pronounced "mul tee yoo zer touring test" (/ˌmʌlti ˌjuːzər ˈtʊrɪŋ ˌtɛst/). humans&'s user-model eval where an LLM judge tells all-human group chat from simulated; Turing as TOOR-ing.

entry.title: NVFP4 — N V F P four
entry.summary: NVFP4 is pronounced "N V F P four" (/ˌɛn viː ɛf piː ˈfɔr/). NVIDIA's 4-bit floating-point format (E2M1 values, E4M3 block scales) on Blackwell/Rubin; read letter-by-letter like other precision initialisms.

entry.title: Astra — astruh
entry.summary: Astra is pronounced "astruh" (/ˈæstrə/). OpenAI's GPT-6 flagship family (Sep 2026); Latin for star, anglicized AS-truh like astral, with the Latin AH-strah as the alternate.

entry.title: DeepInfer — deep infer
entry.summary: DeepInfer is pronounced "deep infer" (/ˈdiːp ɪnˌfɜːr/). DeepSeek's open-source large-scale inference framework (Oct 2026); said as the ordinary words "deep" + "infer".

entry.title: Jev — jev
entry.summary: Jev is pronounced "jev" (/dʒɛv/). TypeSafe AI's decision model; the launch FAQ derives it from economist William Stanley Jevons, so one syllable "jev".

entry.title: Postman — post man
entry.summary: Postman is pronounced "post man" (/ˈpoʊstˌmən/). API platform named for the mail carrier; ordinary English compound POHST-man.

entry.title: Miles — miles
entry.summary: Miles is pronounced "miles" (/maɪlz/). RadixArk's open-source RL post-training framework; the README tagline confirms the ordinary English word reading.

entry.title: CooperBench — cooper bench
entry.summary: CooperBench is pronounced "cooper bench" (/ˈkuːpər ˌbɛntʃ/). Stanford/SAP benchmark scoring AI coding agents as teammates; ordinary English compound Cooper + bench.

entry.title: Four Over Six — four over six
entry.summary: Four Over Six is pronounced "four over six" (/fɔːr ˈoʊvər ˌsɪks/). NVFP4 block-scaling technique (caps block maxima at ±4 vs FP8's ±6); creators spell it as plain English words, read literally.
